O18 (2026-09-06): owner request — enable USDT as a real second direct on-chain payment method alongside native TON, faster/cheaper than NOWPayments. Discovered that src/services/ton-service.ts's own top comment already promised this ('Native TON / USDT-TON payment rail') and the deposit-info text already said 'TON/USDT-TON', but scanTonDeposits() only ever parsed plain TON transfers — USDT-TON was a genuinely unbuilt promise. Implemented the missing half: sending a Jetton (USDT₮ on TON) to the hot wallet doesn't move TON directly, it fires a transfer_notification message (op 0x7362d09c) from the hot wallet's own deterministic USDT-jetton-wallet child contract BACK to the hot wallet itself — so it shows up in the exact same getTransactions() call already used for native TON, no new polling target needed. Added: parsing that notification (amount + forward_payload comment, same memo scheme as native TON), a security check that the message's source address matches the hot wallet's own real USDT jetton-wallet address (computed once via the USDT master contract's get_wallet_address get-method, cached) — rejects any other/fake jetton pretending to be USDT — and crediting at ~1:1 USD (no price-API lookup needed, unlike TON). USDT master contract address (EQCxE6mUtQJKFnGfaROTKOt1lZbDiiX1kCixRv7Nw2Id_sDs) verified via WebSearch cross-referenced against Tether's own supported-protocols page and Tonscan; overridable via USDT_JETTON_MASTER_ADDRESS without a code change. Applied identically (per the established 'deliberately duplicated, never shared' convention) to all 3 files with a shared hot wallet: src/services/ton-service.ts (AD_BOT), marriageTonService.ts, jobsTonService.ts — each keeps crediting its own bot-specific table only. Schema: TonTransaction gets a new `asset` column (TON|USDT, default TON) — migration_22_usdt_ton_deposits.sql; MatchTransaction/JobsTransaction needed no schema change (their `currency` field was already freeform). Updated deposit button labels/instructions in all 3 bots + AD_BOT's i18n strings to say 'TON / USDT' and warn against sending USDT from a non-TON network (TRC20/ERC20) to this address. NOVA_BOT's $5/mo subscription intentionally NOT touched — different product shape (fixed subscription via NOWPayments only, no wallet/balance concept), flagged as a possible future extension rather than silently expanded into. MEDICAL_BOT has no payment surface by design, unaffected. npx tsc --noEmit and npm run build both clean (same pre-existing sandbox-only /sitemap.xml failure as O13, unrelated).

O13 (2026-09-05): owner asked why 'npm run build' fails locally with 'supabaseUrl is required' — investigated instead of dismissing it as env-only noise. Found 2 real bugs: /api/admin/analytics and /api/admin/orders GET routes had no request-scoped input (no cookies/headers/searchParams), so Next.js's app router silently treated them as static-eligible and would bake their DB response into the build output — the admin dashboard's analytics/orders would freeze at build-time data instead of staying live. Fixed with export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic' on both (SHA 8ac7f71). Also added revalidate=30 to sitemap.ts (matches page.tsx/service/[slug] ISR window) so new services appear without a redeploy. The remaining sitemap.xml build failure in THIS sandbox is NOT a code bug — this session has no Supabase credentials at all (confirmed: no .env.local, no SUPABASE_* in the shell env), so sitemap.ts's build-time Supabase fetch can never succeed here regardless of code; Vercel's real build has the real credentials and always succeeds. Swept every other GET route.ts for the same static-freeze risk — none found.
